[message_id=690689 author=EISLab_hwlee first=True]
I would like to bring the community's attention to a deceptive practice currently happening in the notebooks section to farm upvotes.
nvidianemotron 0.81 new making 0.85 public soon 
Why this notebook is fake and deceptive: 
Output Copying (Plagiarism): The code inside this notebook is completely fake and does not generate the score it claims through actual modeling. Instead, it simply copies the submission.zip or outputs from other hard-working Kagglers' top-performing public notebooks directly into /kaggle/working/ . 
Clickbait Titles: The author intentionally uses misleading titles like "making 0.85 public soon" to deceive users and farm upvotes. Furthermore, they have a history of writing fabricated scores in the titles that are completely different from what the actual code inside achieves.
Disabled Comments: To prevent anyone from pointing out these issues or warning others, the author has deliberately disabled the comments section on the notebook.
This behavior disrespects the hard work of original authors and clutters the platform with spam. 
Please be careful, always check the code before upvoting, and let's not reward this kind of cheating behavior.

[message_id=3440609 author=CPMP first=False]
I have proposed to allow downvotes on notebooks for fighting plagiarism, see https://www.kaggle.com/discussions/product-feedback/76394 
It was rejected by Kaggle. Maybe if enough people support this request then it will be implemented.
I think it would be much simpler and more effective than finger pointing posts like yours. Even though I agree with why you posted it.

[message_id=3440614 author=EISLab_hwlee first=False]
Thank you! I totally agree that a downvote button is the best solution, and I just upvoted your proposal. Since the author disabled comments, making this post was the only way to warn others right now. I really hope Kaggle implements your idea soon!

[message_id=3440635 author=CPMP first=False]
Well, my suggestion is 7 years old…

I appreciate the community calling this out.
